On Sun, Jan 10, 2027 at 09:12 AM Amy Zhao <amy.zhao@stellarretail.com> wrote:
> We started seeing a sharp increase in latency across our hosted calls to Redwood around 09:10 PST...

Thanks for the traces — we've started an immediate investigation. Initial findings from our hosted control plane and the serving runtime:

- Symptom window matches an automated housekeeping job that ran at 09:08 PST. After that job, we observe a rapid drop in prefix-index cache hit-rate for the affected shard(s) used by Stellar Retail. Hit-rate fell from ~97% to ~56% (measured by our prefix-hit telemetry).
- The runtime fell back to uncached KV lookups for many requests; avg KV lookups per request rose ~3x. This correlates with the p95/p99 jumps.
- Error spike appears driven by request timeouts while waiting on cold KV fetches; 500s are transient and surface when backend calls timed out under heavy cold-load.
- Host-level metrics: network and GPU utilization are normal; there is no upstream model failure. This looks like a cache-locality regression, not model quality.

Hypothesis: an automated TTL trimming job had its threshold misapplied to a small set of prefix buckets, triggering a targeted purge (we're calling it a prefix-index purge) that caused an eviction storm and an unusually large cold-KV fanout.

What we're doing now (actionable items):
1) Immediately pinned the affected shard to a conservative TTL policy (disable the aggressive purge) — change deployed at 09:38 PST.
2) Running an accelerated rewarm process for hot prefixes (dispatched 09:42 PST) to refill frequently used prefix entries before user traffic ramps.
3) Temporarily increased request-level timeouts for Stellar Retail to reduce 500s while warmup completes.
4) Collecting traces and running a differential analysis across tenants to confirm scope.

Preliminary numbers after mitigation steps: p95 improved to ~240ms by 10:20 PST, p99 ~680ms; error rate down to ~0.6%. Still above baseline but trending to normal.

We'll keep the bridge open and post updates. Full RCA will follow; for immediate needs let's schedule an executive briefing if the customer requests it.

— Evelyn Hart
SRE — Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

Subject: Follow-up: Mitigation summary and next steps — Stellar Retail incident (Jan 10)

Amy — thanks again for the collaboration the past 48 hours. Summary and concrete next steps: 

What happened (short): an automated TTL-trimming housekeeper applied a threshold too aggressively to a subset of prefix-index buckets, causing a targeted purge. The purge produced a short-lived eviction storm that increased backend KV fanout and produced the p95/p99 regressions you observed.

Immediate mitigations we executed:
- Disabled aggressive TTL trimming for affected shard clusters and rolled a conservative TTL policy (deployed 09:38 1/10).
- Deployed accelerated rewarm job to prepopulate hot prefixes for your traffic pattern (started 09:42 1/10).
- Raised request timeouts for your tenant during warmup window to reduce transient 500s.

Status now: service metrics for your tenant are within acceptable ranges — p95/p99 back within SLO targets for the majority of traffic. We continue to monitor for residual perturbations.

Next actions / timeline:
- Postmortem with timeline and root-cause analysis (Rishi/Evelyn) — draft by Jan 18.
- Permanent mitigations: add a canary and stricter threshold validation for TTL trimming jobs, automatic rewarm detection, and a preflight that aborts purges if a shard shows >10% sudden hit-rate drop (engineering plan by Jan 25).
- Executive brief scheduled for Jan 12 at 17:00 PT (per your availability) — Sean will lead.

We take incidents like this seriously and will share the full RCA and code-level remediation once complete. In the meantime, please let us know if you see any regressions — I'll keep the bridge open for a bit longer today.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
